I've ported the program to Zig. `node check.mjs` passes all 5 example cases, both in this directory and in a clean copy. The 9 unit tests pass as well. I also compared the Zig output byte for byte with the original TypeScript program on three 1,000,000-command inputs and a 20,000-line input full of malformed lines. All four matched, and each large input ran in about 0.06 s or less.

- **`src/lru.zig`**: the cache. Lookups go through the standard library's array-backed hash map, and a linked list
